newsitem.title: CANADA: B.C. forest companies' timber costs seen falling.
newsitem.headline: B.C. forest companies' timber costs seen falling.

text.p: Changes in logging rules for British Columbia forestry companies could lower their timber costs by close to six percent or around C$355 million, according to an industry estimate released Tuesday.

The Forest Alliance of British Columbia said the revisions announced Monday could reduce logging costs by as much as C$5 a meter. A recent analysis by consultants KPMG estimated the cost of a delivered cubic meter of wood at C$86.74 in 1996.
With an annual harvest of about 71 million cubic meters, the companies could save around C$355 million based on the alliance's C$5 a meter estimate.

The government said Monday it could not project the value of the savings but was confident the changes would lower costs for both industry and the government. The revisions in the Forest Practices Code, introduced two years ago, were aimed at reducing paperwork and streamlining administration.
Forest companies welcomed the moves while environmentalists said they would undermine logging standards.
